bent: Prithee hear the tuneful fry of the briny deep, whose ceaseless ditty chargeth young and old to dance; e'en the eldest shark joins in the chant.
A gallant from the southern district, opulent in mien, dost strut and prance in gay abandon, teaching all the world his jaunty equestrian jig.
Two dames of the court do boast in ribald rhyme of the riches of their boudoir, that none may doubt their dominion o'er the household arts.
A cowboy rideth to the old town lane, his steed at full gallop, and naught may stay him, for he cannot tarry though the road be long.
Sing slowly, my sweet, that love may savor every passing moment; tarry with me, for desire waxeth and my heart beateth in languorous time.
I come from the city's upper quarter, where I strut with wondrous flair; my style cannot be matched, and all the town dost groove to my bold refrain.
When joy alighteth in my breast, naught can bring me low; I clap my hands and dance upon the air, for happiness hath claimed this heart of mine.
I fell for a maiden in a tavern hall, drawn by her comely form; we dallied through the night, and now my heart doth follow where she goes.
The city's lamps do blind mine eyes, yet I cannot sleep, for I am consumed with longing; I must see my love again ere the dawn.
Thou thinkest thyself the rogue of the realm, but prithee look again; I am the greater villain, and thy mischief is but child's play to mine.
Thou didst betray this heart, and from the depths of my sorrow riseth a storm of vengeance; thou shalt rue the day thou played me false.
I hear thou art wed and happy now; grant me but one boon, that I may find another soul as dear, though tears still fall for thee.
Give me all of thy heart, and I shall give thee all of mine; our flaws and follies intertwined, we shall love without reserve.
No more shall I conceal my icy power; the storm is mine to command, and I stand apart, queen of my own cold dominion.
Are we but shallow creatures adrift upon the tide? Dive with me into the deep, where the waters do not wound as they do near the shore.
I have done a grievous deed and now must pay the price; farewell, good world, though nothing truly matters in the end.
I sought a lodging for the night and found a hostelry most strange; thou mayst check in at any hour, but never mayst thou leave its halls.
Her tresses bring to mind a sunlit field, and her smile is the sweetest sight mine eyes have seen; prithee, sweet child, stay with me.
A lonely soul from the city's edge boards a night train bound for anywhere; hold fast to thy hope, for the journey hath but begun.
A fair lady claimeth I am the father of her child, but the babe resembleth me not; she is no true love, and I must deny her suit.
When darkness falleth and the moon is high, the dead do rise and dance upon the graveyard green; beware the midnight hour, lest thou join their revel.
Thou hadst best take thy leave, for a quarrel brews upon the street; better to walk away than to fall in blood for pride.
A villain smooth of tongue hath broken into her chamber; the maiden lieth stricken, and the culprit glideth away with ne'er a trace.
They name me base and wicked, but I answer that I am the best; from the wrong side of town I prove my worth, and I am bad, and proud.
I never meant to bring thee sorrow; I would walk with thee through the violet downpour and ne'er see thee weep again.
How canst thou leave me when I need thee most? Even the doves above lament our parting, and their cry echoeth in my lonely heart.
When I kneel in supplication, thy voice answereth from the deep; thou art my guiding star, and every whisper sets my soul aflame.
Do not bow to another's will, dear heart; speak thy mind and show the world the truth of thy desires, lest thou live a life that is not thine.
When the world hath brought thee low, strike a pose most grand; let thy spirit take the floor and dance as if the stage were all the world.
Some suitors court me with sweet words alone, but I am no fool; I dwell in a world where gold and baubles speak louder than love's protestations.
Thou hast touched my heart anew and made me feel as though this love were fresh and chaste, as if I knew not passion ere we met.
Papa, chide me not, for I am with child; I shall keep this babe and wed my love, and I pray thou dost stand by me in this hour.
I dreamed I dwelt upon a fair isle where the sea kissed golden sands; though the land be far, my heart remaineth there forever.
Time passeth, yet I remain ensnared in thoughts of thee; every moment I tarry, my longing groweth, and I cannot free myself from this web.
Thy love is a poison most sweet, intoxicating all my senses; though I know it shall undo me, I crave another draught of thee.
My loneliness hath grown beyond bearing; prithee, show me thy heart once more, for I would have thee call upon me yet again.
Forsooth, I have played the wanton once more and toyed with a heart that loved me true; forgive me, for I know not why I do such mischief.
I am a spirit pent within a vessel, and my powers lie sleeping; release me but with gentle hands, and I shall grant a wish most rare.
Though my words may stumble, my hips speak truth; no tongue need untangle this mystery, for the dance declareth all.
When the tempest rageth and the heavens weep, I shall be thy shelter; beneath my wing thou shalt stay dry, for I am ever thine.
My mind doth harbor terrors in the dark; a fever creepeth through my dreams, and I cannot tell if I wake or sleep.
Come, my unruly gallant, and prove thy mettle; I have grown weary of fine words, so show me the passion thou dost boast of.
I desire to be the sole lady of thy regard, the sun about which thy world doth turn; love me as though none other existeth.
In a place most hopeless, where none would seek it, we found love; though the world may frown, our hearts are bound in desperate joy.
Shine bright as the sun's own rays; we are as diamonds in the sky, and none can dim our luster, for we blaze together.
I need thee to remain though I know not why; do not leave me, for in this tangled love thy presence is my only anchor.
I toil from dawn to dusk and yet thy heart remaineth cold; I have worked for this love and found but weary bones.
I am a queen of noble Southern blood, and I bow to none; my lineage, my pride, my fortune, I wear them all like a crown.
If thou didst desire this hand, thou shouldst have placed a ring upon it; I am content alone, and I shall dance with my sisters, needing no suitor.
Thy gaze hath addled my wits; I am a woman possessed, for thy love hath made me mad with longing.
I can spy thy radiance circling round me; I have found my way into thy light, and I shall ne'er let thee fall.
Thou mayst gather thy belongings and begone, for I have no need of thee; there be a thousand like thee in the town, to the left, to the left.
Let no man doubt a woman's might; though I am fair, my strength commandeth all, and my reign shall not be questioned.
I am busy, honey, prithee cease thy calling; I shall ring thee back, for I cannot speak with thee now, for mine ears are full of dance.
I play my hand with countenance most cool; though my heart be aflutter, none may read my game, for I hold a royal flush of wiles.
I crave a love that is ill-fated and dark; I want thy wicked embrace, thy bitter end, thy passion, for I desire what is not good for me.
I have lost all care and shall dance the night away; my head spins and my feet move, and though I know not where I am, I shall not stop.
I was made in this wise, and I hold my head high; no man's judgment may undo me, for I am right and proud to be as nature formed me.
A suitor's name I dare not speak, yet he haunteth my every thought; though this passion is my ruin, I cannot banish him from my heart.
I am a wanton who shall betray again, for I love a man whom I know to be my doom; I cannot help myself, for I kiss the serpent's mouth.
I live for the thunder of clapping hands; my soul thirsteth for the crowd's acclaim, and I would die upon the stage ere I forgo their praise.
Though heaven weepeth upon me, I shall not be drowned; pour down thy sorrows, for I have wept enough, and let the deluge find me standing.
This love is foolish, yet I must have it; I seek a companion who will love me without shame, for I have need of foolish, honest love.
My mind is my own undoer; I am caught in a fever of the soul and beg for aid, yet no physician can cure what aileth this heart.
I am a sweetmeat with a bitter core; taste me not unless thou canst bear the tang, for I am sour candy wrapped in honey.
If the world should end this very night, I would not fret so long as I hold thee close; I would perish with a smile upon my lips.
Thou hast cast a spell upon my heart; with a word most strange thou hast ensnared me, and with one charm my will is gone.
Hark, the winter chill descendeth and my rhymes flow cold as frost; if there be trouble, I shall meet it, for I am the chillest bard in the land.
Come, maidens and gallants, and take my hand; I shall teach thee a dance most merry that all the world dost sway to, so give thy body joy.
Haters shall say what they will, but I shall shake their words from my shoulders and dance on, for their spite cannot touch this heart.
